non_blocking: No ABANDON: after about ten searches (web plus arxiv.org/aclanthology fetches) I found no paper containing the main result (pooled pick with NONE vs isolated verification, matched confidence-based lineup ROC, base-rate instruction not moving the criterion, forced pick = most-accepted wrong candidate, same-family verifier not catching it). Absence of a hit is not proof; searches were keyword-limited.

Closest uncited-or-thinly-cited neighbours to add or position against: Tam et al. 2025 'None of the Above, Less of the Right' (ACL Findings 2025, aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.1031; arXiv 2503.01550), which reports that NOTA-as-correct options cause a 30-50% drop and that models struggle to reject all options; this is uncited and bears directly on the 'NONE option' claim. Kim & Jung 2026 (arXiv 2610.08153) is cited but only briefly: it removes the correct option from MMLU-Pro math MCQA and offers ABSTAIN, so it is the nearest math, no-valid-option precedent; the paper should say explicitly it does not compare pooled choosing against isolated verification.

Wixted & Mickes-style SDT/ROC analysis of lineup procedures is the method lineage; arXiv 2603.14893 ('LLMs as Signal Detectors', ROC from confidence bins for LLMs) and arXiv 2609.18204 (cited as chen2026beyond; SDT criterion shift in LLM overseers) show SDT framing of LLM judges is not new. The paper credits only the latter; the novelty claim should be limited to applying the lineup procedure contrast (pooled vs isolated, target-absent), not to the SDT framing.

Related-work characterisations checked and accurate: wang2025llms (arXiv 2402.01349 abstract and Table 3: incorrect options with highest confidence reach 83.6% to 99.4% of the correct option's confidence; NOTA replacement drops performance); rho2025best (arXiv 2510.04087 abstract: 'selecting the least bad of many unacceptable options', outside option); ma2026selecting (arXiv 2611.00507, selection vs solving, workshop); ji2026candidate (arXiv 2608.25937; 'All-wrong pools were excluded (Fig. 4c)' in the full text, matching the paper); chen2026beyond (arXiv 2609.18204, criterion shift via SDT); kim2026penalty (arXiv 2610.08153). Minor wording: chen2026 found a shift toward rejection and more false alarms, so 'criterion rather than detection effects' is right but the direction is opposite to this paper's liberal shift and could be stated.

Not verifiable by me: zhang2026selected (paper says only the abstract was read, which is honest) and the HICSS/AACL venue notes taken from arXiv comments. The sentence that wang2025llms 'models often still choose an option when the correct one is replaced and a no-answer option is offered' is a fair paraphrase but their 'None of the Above' result is an accuracy drop, not a choice rate; consider softening.

Claim 'Eyewitness research predicts...' in the abstract is framed as a prior; Wells 1984 and Malpass & Devine 1981 are the right sources, but the paper's own results (J not detectably lower, ROC indistinguishable) cut against the strict relative-judgment prediction, which the text already concedes.
